posts.title: I measured dev.to's engagement layer. 92% of posts get zero reactions, and the good comments aren't people.
posts.tldr: Two independent audits and a 460-post sample show that dev.to's engagement layer is largely machine-shaped. The practical consequence for anyone publishing there: stop optimising for reactions, because the number is farmable.

posts.title: A free AI chat that costs me nothing: BYOK on Cloudflare Workers AI
posts.tldr: Every user brings their own Workers AI token. The operator pays nothing, the quota is theirs, and the hard part isn't the auth — it's stripping your own directives out of a live token stream.

posts.title: I ship open-source security tools solo — here's the full stack, the pricing, and the (zero) revenue so far
posts.tldr: A solo dev's transparent monetization setup: MIT-licensed security tooling, two paid products ($50 Talus Enterprise pack, $29 Externum Pro Pack), and the honest zero-revenue-so-far report.

posts.title: Externum: a typed language that transpiles to Python and Bash — and its own benchmark caught two real bugs
posts.tldr: One typed source, three backends: readable Python, standalone Bash, and a .exbc artifact that runs without source. Honest design trade-offs, a hyperfine benchmark, and the two bytecode-VM bugs the benchmark itself caught — fixed same day.

posts.title: Detecting ransomware with eBPF in Rust
posts.tldr: A working-code tutorial on building a ransomware detector in Rust with eBPF: kernel tracepoints, perf buffers, sliding-window detection, and automated SIGKILL response.

posts.title: A web OS that 'never booted': the two bugs that looked like kernel failures but were 404s and z-index
posts.tldr: Aurora 'stuck on kernel init' was dist/ being gitignored (GitHub Pages serves the repo, not your build output) — and the follow-up 'icons don't click' was a full-bleed z-index:2 overlay swallowing pointer events. Two boring bugs, two days of 'the OS is broken'.

posts.title: Building a Solana-like validator in Rust: what PoH, Tower BFT and Sealevel actually force you to think about
posts.tldr: Re-implementing a Solana-like node in Rust teaches more than the whitepaper does: the PoH clock is a schedule problem, Tower BFT is a voting-height game, and Sealevel parallelism lives or dies on account locks.

posts.title: eBPF verifier limits are a design constraint: what CO-RE field offsets and bounded loops taught me
posts.tldr: The eBPF verifier is not a linter you appease — it's a constraint you design around. CO-RE field offsets break across kernel versions, bounded loops force you to restructure agents, and the verification story has to live in CI, not in your head.

posts.title: I made my portfolio readable to AI crawlers: llms.txt, JSON-LD and a 40-method distribution stack
posts.tldr: llms.txt + JSON-LD entity graphs + IndexNow make a zero-budget GitHub Pages site citable by answer engines, and a git-push pipeline cross-posts every article to 9 platforms for free.

posts.title: Catching ransomware with eBPF: what execve/openat tracing taught me about false positives
posts.tldr: Behavioural eBPF tracing (execve/openat + per-CPU perf buffers) catches ransomware by the shape of its damage — the hard part is scoring patterns without crying wolf on every cargo build.
